RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT (Massachusetts) — synthetic test fixture (KITCHEN SINK)

This is a fabricated lease used only for testing the LeaseLookout Massachusetts
ruleset. It is NOT a real lease and must NOT be used by any tenant or landlord.
Every clause below is deliberately abusive and is planted to trip exactly one
rule. Statute fingerprint for the parser: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

1. Parties and Premises. This Lease is made between the Landlord and the Tenant for the residential premises located in Boston, Massachusetts.

2. Term. The term of this Lease is twelve (12) months, beginning September 1.

3. Rent. The Tenant shall pay the monthly rent on the first day of each calendar month.

4. Security Deposit Amount. The Tenant shall pay a security deposit of two months' rent before taking occupancy.

5. Handling of Deposit. The Landlord may commingle the security deposit with the Landlord's own funds and general operating accounts.

6. Deposit Interest. The security deposit shall not bear interest of any kind for the benefit of the Tenant.

7. Return of Deposit. The Landlord shall return the deposit within forty-five (45) days after the Tenant vacates.

8. Deposit Character. The first month's payment labeled herein is a non-refundable security deposit and will not be returned under any circumstances.

9. Late Fees. A late fee of $75 shall be charged after five (5) days if rent is not paid when due.

10. Application Fee. Each applicant shall pay a non-refundable application fee of $50 before the application is processed.

11. Move-In Fee. The Tenant shall pay a non-refundable move-in fee prior to occupancy in addition to the amounts above.

12. Condition. The Tenant accepts the premises in its present condition and waives the implied warranty of habitability.

13. Liability. The Tenant agrees to indemnify and hold the Landlord harmless from any and all liability for injury occurring on the premises.

14. Jury. The Tenant agrees to waive any right to a trial by jury in any dispute with the Landlord.

15. Constructive Eviction. The parties agree that no action or failure to act by the Landlord shall be construed as a constructive eviction.

16. Default Remedies. Upon default, the Landlord may lock the tenant out and shut off the utilities without resort to any court.

17. Complaints. The Landlord may retaliate against the Tenant for reporting any condition to the board of health.

18. Entry. The Landlord may enter the premises at any time and for any reason without notice to the Tenant.

19. Early Termination. The Tenant shall forfeit the deposit if the Tenant elects early termination of this Lease.

20. Quiet Enjoyment. The Tenant is entitled to the quiet enjoyment of the premises throughout the term.
